- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.3) — especially after recent spikes — and adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Underestimate prices during strong negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.5) — model tends to ignore downside risk; increase forecast slightly to account for mean reversion or policy-driven support.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days) — model reacts too aggressively; cap forecast peak at 1.5–2x recent high or use 10-day moving average as ceiling.
- Lag in price correction after negative sentiment — model often delays downward adjustment; apply early correction if sentiment drops below -0.4.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 20% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts overestimate if sentiment is volatile (±0.3+ in last 5 days) — use 20-day smoothed average as anchor.
